mechanism: Both drugs are metabolized by hepatic CYP450 enzymes (tolterodine by CYP2D6/3A4, albendazole by CYP1A1/2C9), with potential for competitive inhibition and altered metabolism; albendazole may also enhance tolterodine's anticholinergic effects through additive pharmacodynamic actions.
action: Monitor for increased anticholinergic symptoms (dry mouth, urinary retention, constipation, cognitive effects); consider dose adjustment of tolterodine if toxicity occurs; ensure adequate hepatic function assessment.
